subject: Tenancy risk assessment and canary rollout plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Tenancy risk assessment and canary rollout plan

Asha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps so both sides are aligned. TL;DR: we recommend a short canary on Dedicated capacity before any move to Private VPC (if you want long-term isolation).

What we covered:
- Helix priority: predictable tail latency for realtime patient-facing inference (95th/99th p95/p99 targets) and clear isolation for PHI workloads.
- Options: Hosted API (fast onboarding), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool w/ tenant isolation), Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem for maximum control).
- Primary concern you raised: "noisy neighbor" impacts on p99 under spiky load and auditability for compliance.

Proposed immediate plan (actionable):
1) Proof-of-Concept (2-week) — Dedicated pool canary: small reserved pool (2-4 GPUs), enforced tenancy, network allowlist, and traceable request IDs. Run with Helix test traffic and a 10% sample of production traffic if you want realism.
2) SLOs and observability — define p95/p99 targets, token-cost budget, and alert thresholds. We will enable request-level latency sampling, token breakdown, and per-route dashboards.
3) Rollout & fallback — start with Dedicated canary; if isolation or latency still exposes issues, escalate to Private VPC (we’ll provide a clear migration checklist).
4) Contract & evidence — we’ll share a short appendix with tenancy guarantees, SOC2 summary, and a draft canary run template.

Next steps / owners:
- Helix: confirm who will provide the test dataset and whether the sample can include live traffic (Asha) — due Tue 11/17.
- Redwood: attach tenancy appendix + canary template (Ben) — sent in followup email.
- Infra deep-dive: we’ll have Karthik and Jordan run a quick design session if you opt into the dedicated canary.

Attachments: redwood-tenancy-appendix.pdf (summary of isolation controls), canary-rollout-template.xlsx (runbook + metrics).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if any of the steps above need clarifying.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Tenancy risk assessment and canary rollout plan

Ben — appreciate the summary, this is very helpful. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we lock the canary:

1) What exactly do you mean by "enforced tenancy" on Dedicated? Is it instance-level isolation or do GPUs still multiplex different customers at the hypervisor level? We need to know where the noisy neighbor risk remains.
2) For the canary, we cannot put PHI in a test cluster. Can your telemetry operate on synthetic traffic that matches our production QPS/sequence-length distribution?
3) What SLOs do you normally guarantee for Dedicated runs during a canary? We want to be sure the 99th latency will be stable for the user journey that is < 200ms now.

Procurement: please advise on any PO/contract constraints that would block a short paid POC.

-Asha
Asha Patel
Director of Engineering, Helix Health
asha.patel@helixhealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@helixhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenancy risk assessment and canary rollout plan

Asha — quick follow from the infra side. Short answers first:

- "Enforced tenancy" (what Ben described) = tenant-local inference queues with dedicated GPU assignment for the reserved pool. We do not mix inference work from multiple customers on the same dedicated GPU in that pool during the reservation period. That removes typical noisy neighbor vectors caused by mixed-tenant batching.
- Under the Dedicated reserved pool we still share host OS and some orchestration services; however, inference processes and CUDA contexts are isolated per-tenant. We can provide kernel-level telemetry to show process-level GPU utilization during the canary.

About PHI and synthetic traffic: absolutely — our telemetry supports replayed synthetic traffic that preserves your production distribution (tokens/sequence lengths) without including raw PHI. We can run a short profiling pass to validate the distribution match.

SLOs: during a customer canary on Dedicated we operate under a "best-effort" latency SLX in the contract but can set explicit alerting thresholds for p95 and p99. For your use-case (target p99 <= 200ms) we recommend the canary run at your peak 99th load for 48 hours to validate tail behavior. If we fail to meet the threshold during canary, we will classify the run as "failed canary" and propose Private VPC options for stricter isolation.

I'll volunteer to own the telemetry dashboard for the canary and produce a post-mortem with token-level cost and latency breakdowns.

-Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@helixhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenancy risk assessment and canary rollout plan

Asha — adding more detail on the technical playbook for the Dedicated canary and a proposed canary run config. I know you asked for specifics so your security and SRE teams can evaluate risk.

Canary configuration (proposed):
- Duration: 14 days (we recommend minimum 7 days, prefer 14 for weekly usage patterns).
- Pool size: start 2 GPUs (a1-large equiv), scale to 4 if peak 99th is higher than expected.
- Routing: explicit ingress allowlist from Helix subnets + mTLS between Helix client and the dedicated endpoints.
- Isolation: dedicated CUDA contexts per-tenant in the reserved pool, no cross-tenant batching, and per-tenant KV cache.
- Observability: per-request tracing id, token-level latency, model KV cache hit rate, GPU power draw and kernel time. Dashboards will show p50/p95/p99 and request error breakdowns.
- Failure criteria: >1.5x increase in p99 vs baseline for 30m, or sustained error-rate >0.5% for 1h.
- Rollback path: immediate traffic shift to Hosted (read-only) endpoints or back to your prior inference stack while we open an incident. If the canary fails due to tail latency we recommend transitioning to Private VPC with dedicated hosts (no shared orchestration plane).

Security/compliance notes:
- SOC2 artifacts: we can share our SOC2 summary and mapping doc; full attestation available under NDA.
- Audit logs: request-level logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure push for the canary window.

I'll attach a canonical canary-rollout-template.xlsx in a follow-up (already attached to Ben's original mail) and I can run the infra design session with your SREs this week.

-karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
